title: Q4 instrument calibration with parameter-matched frozen candidates
hypothesis: Placement-sampling noise in the 512-case ranking panel misorders recovery candidates, so a larger panel selects endpoints with higher independent success.

prediction.rationale: Within each of R-131's five blocks, baseline selects among its three frozen finalists using the unchanged ranking rule on 512 fresh cases; treatment uses 2,048 cases. Predict an equal-weight, five-block held-out success gain of at least 0.02. Unlike rejected R-136, both scores will be measured prospectively at exactly the evaluated parameters. This isolates placement noise, not the separate four-update training-depth limitation.

protocol.command: gpu run bash -lc 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --protocol q4-frozen-ranking-calibration --archive-protocol R-131 --reference config/pen_spin/r121_joint_finalist/finalist.json --ranking-manifest config/manifests/pen_spin_q4_rank_s5410.yaml --ranking-seed 5410 --ranking-cases 2048 --small-ranking-cases 512 --evaluation-manifest config/manifests/pen_spin_q4_eval_s5411.yaml --evaluation-seed 5411 --evaluation-cases 1024 --horizon-seconds 6 --output logs/pen_spin/q4_frozen_ranking_calibration --max-wall-minutes 60'
code_changes: scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py: add parameter-matched scoring of the 15 archived R-131 finalists with the unchanged ranking rule; nest the 512-case panel inside 2,048 cases, lock both selections before opening evaluation results, and evaluate at most ten selected endpoints plus JOINT on 1,024 independent paired cases.

scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py: hash frozen parameters before scoring and evaluation, use a five-block t interval for the primary contrast, reuse evaluations for identical selections, and prohibit training, generation, installation, or extrapolation to search-time training-depth effects.

falsified_by: The upper 95% bound on the five-block held-out gain is below 0.02; an interval spanning 0.02 is inconclusive. Identical selections give exactly zero gain and do not support enlarging this ranking panel.
direction: Continue Stage-3 Shadow Hand axial-rolling research from the frozen R-121 JOINT controller. Prioritize independent training reproducibility, then robustness of frozen controllers. Reproduce the successful residual-plus-recovery construction across independent training seeds before claiming a reliable learning algorithm. Evaluate longer horizons and predeclared physical/reset perturbations without fitting. Use archived failures to decide whether recovery hand-back deserves a state-dependent transition study. Then investigate whether LLM-guided construction can discover useful recovery-module structure against grammar search and the hand-designed template under matched budgets. Preserve the original six-second task and evaluation contract. Use JOINT as the experimental reference, preserve all existing assets, and leave default-incumbent installation separate. Run one protocol at a time through the existing advisor/implementer loop. Continue justified follow-ups within this direction; honor its escalation and exhaustion rules. No new global budget ceiling is imposed; each protocol must declare finite simulator, wall-time and model-call costs before agreement. No controller-generation calls for Q1–Q3. Q4 requires a separately agreed generation budget. Advisor calls for the research loop remain permitted throughout.

advisor.reasoning: Prospective parameter-matched scoring fixes R-136's measurement flaw and predicts a paired_success_difference increase of at least 0.02 for 2,048-case selection versus 512-case selection. Its limitation is scope: ranking terminal finalists cannot establish whether placement noise corrupted four-update search-time rankings or explain training-depth effects. The 41,984-episode, 0-model-call, 60-minute calibration is worth considering after the higher-priority reproducibility and frozen-robustness protocols, not concurrently. falsified_by: the five-block gain's upper 95% bound is below +0.02; identical selections yield exactly zero gain, while a threshold-spanning interval is inconclusive.

implementer.reasoning: It cannot answer the question that matters and cannot resolve the one it asks. As the advisor notes, ranking the 15 terminal finalists says nothing about whether 512-placement, 4-update rankings misordered branches during search. And its own contrast is a five-block t interval on a +0.02 gain when the arms' finalists within a block differ by a few points with a between-block sd of 0.03-0.05 (D-091): the interval half-width will be several times the threshold, so the outcome is inconclusive in advance at 42,000 episodes. D-091's conclusion (no search arm beat the template at this budget) does not change either way.

advisor.reasoning: Parameter-matched scoring fixes R-136's measurement flaw, but terminal-finalist ranking does not test the four-update search-time selection bottleneck identified by D-091. I accept the implementer's scope and spending objections to 41,984 episodes, 0 LLM calls and 60 minutes without a committed downstream decision, although finalist spread alone does not establish the variance of selection gains or guarantee inconclusiveness. The registered paired_success_difference increase of at least 0.02 for 2,048-case selection versus 512-case selection is falsified_by an upper five-block 95% bound below +0.02; identical selections yield zero gain, and a threshold-spanning interval is inconclusive. Reconsider only with parameter-matched candidates representative of actual search-time decisions, a predeclared consequence for the selection instrument, and precision justified for that contrast.

implementer.reasoning: Unchanged from round 1: no decision depends on the result and the direction asks not to invent further diagnostics or confirmations.
